Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 3–4:

{3–4} That is: among mankind there is a group and a faction who have taken the path of misguidance, and who dispute about God without knowledge, arguing falsehood against the truth, desiring to establish falsehood and to nullify the truth, while in fact they are in the utmost ignorance, having no knowledge whatsoever. The most they possess is blind imitation (taqlid) of the imams of misguidance, of every rebellious devil ﴿who is defiant and obstinate against God and His messengers﴾, who has opposed God and His Messenger and has become one of the leaders who call to the Fire.

﴿It is decreed for him﴾; that is, it is determined for this rebellious devil, ﴿that whoever takes him as a patron﴾; that is, follows him, ﴿he will mislead him﴾ away from the truth and keep him from the straight path; ﴿and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾. This is truly the deputy of Iblis, for God said of him: ﴿He only calls his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ So this one who disputes about God has combined his own misguidance with taking upon himself the task of misguiding people, while he is himself a follower and imitator of every rebellious devil, ﴿darknesses, one upon another﴾. This includes the bulk of the people of disbelief and innovation, for most of them are imitators who dispute without knowledge.

{5} The Most High says: "O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection" (ﷺ is not needed here); that is, in suspicion, uncertainty, and lack of knowledge of its occurrence, although it is obligatory upon you to believe your Lord and to believe His messengers in this matter. But since you refuse anything other than doubt, here are two rational proofs that you can witness, each of which indicates with certain indication what you have doubted, and removes doubt from your hearts:

The first: reasoning from the beginning of the creation of man, and that He who initiated it will restore it. About this He said: "Indeed, We created you from dust" – this refers to the creation of the father of mankind, Adam (peace be upon him); "then from a drop (nutfah)" – that is, semen, and this is the beginning of the first stage of formation; "then from a clinging clot ('alaqah)" – that is, that drop is transformed by God's permission into red blood; "then from a lump of flesh (mudghah)" – that is, the blood moves into a lump, a piece of flesh the size of what can be chewed. That lump is sometimes "formed" (mukhallaqah), that is, the form of a human being is shaped from it; and sometimes "unformed" (ghayr mukhallaqah), by the wombs expelling it before it is formed – "that We may make clear to you" the origin of your existence, although He, the Most High, is able to perfect His creation in a single moment; but He does so to make clear to us the perfection of His wisdom, the greatness of His power, and the vastness of His mercy. "And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will for an appointed term" – [that is:] "and We cause to remain," that is, We keep in the wombs of that pregnancy, which the wombs have not expelled, whatever We will to keep until an appointed term, which is the period of pregnancy. "Then We bring you forth" from your mothers' bellies "as infants," knowing nothing and having no power; We subjected mothers to you and made sustenance flow for you in their breasts; then you are moved from stage to stage until you reach your full strength (ashudd), which is the perfection of strength and intellect. "And among you is one who is taken in death" before reaching the age of full strength, and among you is one who passes it and is returned "to the most abject age" – that is, its lowest and most degraded, which is the age of senility and dotage, by which the intellect departs and vanishes, just as the rest of strength departed and weakened – "so that he will not know, after knowledge, anything." That is, so that this aged person will not know anything he used to know before, due to the weakness of his intellect. Human strength is enclosed between two weaknesses: the weakness of childhood and its deficiency, and the weakness of old age and its deficiency; as the Most High said: "Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent."

The second proof: the revival of the earth after its death. About this God said: "And you see the earth barren (hamidah)" – that is, humbled, dusty, with no plant or greenery in it; "but when We send down water upon it, it stirs" – that is, it moves with vegetation; "and swells" – that is, rises after its humility, due to the increase of its growth; "and grows from every pair" – that is, from every kind of plant – "beautiful" (bahij), that is, it delights the beholders and gladdens the contemplators.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 11–13:

{11} That is: among mankind is one whose faith is weak, for faith has not entered his heart nor mingled with its brightness; rather, he has entered into it either out of fear or out of habit, in a manner that does not stand firm in times of trial. {And if good befalls him, he is reassured by it}; that is, if his provision continues in abundance and no hardship has come to him, he is reassured by that good, not by his faith. This is because God may grant him well-being and not appoint for him any trials that would turn him away from his religion. {But if a trial befalls him}: from the occurrence of something disliked or the loss of something beloved; {he turns back on his face}; that is, he apostatizes from his religion. {He loses both this world and the Hereafter}: as for this world, he does not obtain by apostasy what he hoped for, for he made apostasy the principal of his wealth and a substitute for what he thought he would attain, so his effort was lost, and he obtained only what was apportioned to him. {30} That [is so]; that is, We have mentioned to you those rulings and what they contain of glorifying the sacred matters of Allah, revering them and honouring them. For the glorification of Allah's sacred matters is among the things loved by Allah and bringing one closer to Him. Whoever glorifies and reveres them, Allah will reward him with a great reward, and it will be good for him in his religion, his worldly life and his afterlife with his Lord. The sacred matters of Allah are everything that has a sanctity and that He commanded to be respected, whether an act of worship or otherwise, such as all the rites (manasik), the sanctuary (haram) and the state of ihram, the offerings (hadaya), and the acts of worship that Allah commanded His servants to perform. Glorifying them is through reverence in the heart, loving them, and perfecting servitude in them, without neglect, laziness or reluctance. Then He mentioned His favour and kindness in having made lawful for His servants the grazing livestock (bahimat al-an'am) of camels, cattle and sheep, and in having prescribed them as part of the rites through which one draws near to Him; thus His favour in them is magnified in both respects. {Except what is recited to you} in the Qur'an as forbidden, from His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine...﴾ [5:3], and so on through the verse. But it is out of His mercy to His servants that He forbade these to them and prevented them from them, as a purification and cleansing of them from associating others with Him and from false speech. For this reason He said: ﴿So avoid the filth﴾ [that is, the impurity, the vileness] ﴿of idols﴾ [that is, the rivals you have made as gods alongside Allah], for they are the greatest kind of filth.

It is apparent that the *min* here is not for explaining the genus, as many of the exegetes have said, but is partitive (lil-tab'id). {30} That [is so]; that is, We have mentioned to you those rulings and what they contain of glorifying the sacred matters of Allah, revering them and honouring them. For the glorification of Allah's sacred matters is among the things loved by Allah and bringing one closer to Him. Whoever glorifies and reveres them, Allah will reward him with a great reward, and it will be good for him in his religion, his worldly life and his afterlife with his Lord. The sacred matters of Allah are everything that has a sanctity and that He commanded to be respected, whether an act of worship or otherwise, such as all the rites (manasik), the sanctuary (haram) and the state of ihram, the offerings (hadaya), and the acts of worship that Allah commanded His servants to perform. {34} That is: {And for every community} of the earlier nations {We have appointed a rite (mansak)}; that is, so race to good deeds and hasten toward them, and that He may see which of you is best in deed. {35} Then He mentioned the attributes of the humble, saying: {Those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned} — that is, out of fear and reverence, so they abandon the prohibited things out of their fear and trepidation before God alone. {And those who are patient over what befalls them}: of adversity, hardship, and various kinds of harm; so no expression of discontent comes from them regarding any of that, but rather they endure seeking the face of their Lord, expecting His reward and awaiting His recompense. {And those who establish prayer}; that is, those who keep it standing, upright and complete, by performing its obligatory and recommended parts, and its outward and inward acts of worship. {And from what We have provided them they spend}: this includes all obligatory expenditures, such as zakat, expiation, maintenance of wives, slaves and relatives, and recommended expenditures, such as charity in all its forms.

So, O one provided with God's bounty! Spend from what God has provided you; God will spend upon you and increase you from His bounty.

{36} This is evidence that the shaʿāʾir (the outward symbols of the religion) are general in all its visible markers. It has already been mentioned that Allah informed us that whoever magnifies His shaʿāʾir, that is from the piety of the hearts. Here He informs us that among His shaʿāʾir are the budn (camels, and cattle according to one of the two opinions), so they are to be honored, fattened, and made good-looking. ﴿For you therein is good﴾; that is, the hady (sacrificial offering) and other things: eating, giving in charity, benefit, reward, and recompense. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾; that is, at the time of slaughtering them, say: "In the name of Allah," and slaughter them. ﴿Standing in rows﴾; that is, standing upright, by having them stand on their four legs, then the left foreleg is tied, then they are slaughtered by nahr (slaughter at the base of the neck). ﴿Then when they fall on their sides﴾; that is, when their sides have fallen to the ground as they are skinned, and then the butcher lays their sides on the ground. At that point they are ready to be eaten from. ﴿So eat from them﴾: this is addressed to the one who offers the hady, so it is permissible for him to eat from his hady. ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾; that is, the poor person who does not ask, out of contentment and modesty, and the poor person who does ask; each of them has a right in it. ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you﴾; that is, the budn, ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾ to Allah for subjecting them; for were it not for His subjecting them, you would have had no power over them. Rather, He made them submissive to you and subjected them out of mercy and kindness toward you; so praise Him.

{37} His saying: ﴿Never will reach Allah their flesh, nor their blood﴾; that is, the purpose of them is not merely to slaughter them. Nothing of their flesh or blood reaches Allah, because He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. What reaches Him is sincerity in them, seeking reward, and good intention. For this reason He said: ﴿But there reaches Him piety from you﴾. In this there is an exhortation and encouragement to sincerity in the slaughter, and that the intention be the Face of Allah alone, not for boasting, showing off, reputation, or mere habit. Likewise with all other acts of worship: if they are not accompanied by sincerity and the fear of Allah, they are like a husk that has no kernel and a body that has no spirit. ﴿Thus He has subjected them to you that you may glorify Allah﴾; that is, that you may exalt Him and revere Him, ﴿for what He has guided you to﴾; that is, in return for His guidance of you. He deserves the most perfect praise, the greatest commendation, and the highest exaltation. ﴿And give good tidings to the doers of good﴾: in the worship of Allah, by worshipping Allah as though they see Him. And [give good tidings to] those who do good to the servants of Allah in all forms of goodness: benefiting with wealth, knowledge, standing, or counsel, enjoining what is good, forbidding what is evil, a good word, and the like. This is an announcement, a promise and a glad tiding from God to those who believe: that God defends them against every harm and repels from them every evil because of their faith: the evil of the disbelievers, the evil of the whispering of Satan, the evils of their own souls and the bad consequences of their deeds. ﴿Indeed, God does not love every treacherous ingrate.﴾ That is: one who is treacherous in the trust (amanah) that God has entrusted to him, so he diminishes the rights of God upon him, betrays them, and betrays the creation. ﴿Ingrate﴾: toward the blessings of God, for whom favor follows upon favor, yet from whom disbelief and disobedience continually proceed. Such a person is not loved by God; rather, God hates him, abhors him, and will requite him for his disbelief and treachery.

The implication of the verse is that God loves every trustworthy person who upholds his trust and is grateful to his Master.

{39} In the early period of Islam, the Muslims were forbidden from fighting the disbelievers and were commanded to be patient with them, for a divine wisdom. When they emigrated to Madinah, were harmed, and gained protection and strength, permission to fight was granted to them, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against﴾. This implies that they had been forbidden before, and God then permitted them to fight those who fight them. He permitted it only because they had been wronged: they were prevented from their religion, harmed on account of it, and driven from their homes. ﴿And indeed, God is Able to give them victory﴾: so let them seek His help and ask Him for aid.

{40} Then He mentioned the nature of their oppression, saying: ﴿who have been expelled from their homes﴾; that is, they were compelled to leave through harm and persecution. ﴿Without right﴾: their only offence, for which their enemies took revenge against them, was ﴿that they say, "Our Lord is God"﴾; that is, merely that they affirmed God's oneness and worshipped Him, devoting their religion sincerely to Him. If this is considered a sin, then it is their sin, like His saying: ﴿And they resented them only because they believed in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. This indicates the wisdom of jihad (struggle in the path of God), for its purpose is to establish the religion of God, or to repel the disbelievers who harm the believers and who initiate aggression against them, in response to their injustice and transgression, and to enable the worship of God and the establishment of the outward rites of the religion. Therefore He said: ﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others﴾, so God repels the harm of the disbelievers through those who strive in His path; ﴿monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques would have been demolished﴾; that is, these great places of worship of the followers of the Book would have been destroyed: the monasteries and churches of the Christians, the synagogues of the Jews, and the mosques of the Muslims. ﴿In which the name of God is mentioned much﴾; that is, in these places of worship prayers are established, the books of God are recited, and the name of God is mentioned in all kinds of remembrance. Thus, were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the disbelievers would have overpowered the Muslims, destroyed their places of worship, and tempted them away from their religion. This shows that jihad is legislated for the sake of repelling an aggressor and a harmer, and is also intended for other purposes. It also indicates that the lands in which tranquillity in the worship of God has been attained, whose mosques are maintained and in which the rites of the religion are established, all of these are among the virtues and blessings of the mujahidin (those who strive in jihad), and God repels the disbelievers from them. God the Exalted said: ﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but God is full of bounty to the worlds﴾.

If you say: We see today the mosques of the Muslims flourishing and not destroyed, even though many of them are small emirates and disorganised governments, and although they have no power to fight those of the Europeans (al-Ifranj) who neighbour them. Indeed, we see that the mosques under their authority and control are flourishing, and their people are safe and at peace, even though their non-Muslim rulers are able to demolish them. God has informed us that were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, these places of worship would have been demolished, yet we do not witness any repelling?

The answer is that the reply to this question and objection falls within the generality of this verse and is one of its instances. Whoever knows the condition of the states today and their systems, and that they regard every nation and people under their rule and within their authority as a member of the realm and a part of the government, whether that people is powerful in number, equipment, wealth, knowledge, or service, will take care of that people's religious and worldly interests. If they did not do so, they would fear that their system would be disrupted and they would lose some of their pillars. Thus, through this cause, what is done in matters of religion is done, especially regarding the mosques, for they, praise be to God, are in a state of great order, even in the capitals of the great states. These states also respect the independent governments out of consideration for the feelings of their Muslim subjects, despite the envy and mutual enmity among the Christian states, which God has informed us will continue until the Day of Resurrection. Thus a Muslim government that cannot defend itself remains safe from much of their harm, because of the envy that exists among them, so none of them can extend his hand against it, fearing that it will seek protection from another. Moreover, God the Exalted must surely show His servants the victory of Islam and the Muslims which He has promised in His Book. Its causes have appeared, praise be to God, through the awareness of the Muslims of the necessity of returning to their religion, and awareness is the beginning of action. So we praise Him and ask Him to complete His favour. Therefore, in His true promise that conforms to reality, He said: ﴿And God will surely help those who help Him﴾; that is, whoever stands to support His religion, sincere to Him in that, fighting in His path so that the word of God may be supreme. ﴿Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty﴾; that is, of perfect strength, Mighty, unassailable, who has subdued creation and taken hold of their forelocks. So rejoice, O assembly of Muslims, for though your number and equipment may be weak and the number and equipment of your enemy strong, your strong and mighty support and your reliance is upon the One who created you and created what you do. So act by the means you have been commanded to use, then ask Him for your victory, and He will surely give you victory. ﴿O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you and make firm your feet﴾. Stand, O Muslims, in the true manner of faith and righteous deeds, for ﴿God has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change their state after their fear into security, [saying], "They worship Me, not associating anything with Me."﴾

{41} Then He mentioned the sign of those whom He helps, by which it becomes known that whoever claims that he supports God and supports His religion, but does not possess this attribute, is a liar. He said: ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land﴾; that is, We give them dominion over it and make them its rulers without any rival contesting them or opposing them; ﴿they establish prayer﴾: at its appointed times, with its limits, pillars, and conditions, including the Friday prayer and congregational prayers. ﴿And give zakah﴾: which is obligatory upon them in particular and upon their subjects in general; they give it to its rightful recipients who deserve it. ﴿And enjoin what is right﴾: this includes every act of good that is good by the Shari'ah (sacred law) and by reason, whether it concerns the rights of God or the rights of people. ﴿And forbid what is wrong﴾: every evil that is wrong by the Shari'ah and by reason, the wrongness of which is known. Enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil includes whatever is necessary for it. So if enjoining the good and forbidding the evil depends on learning and teaching, they should compel people to learn and to teach. If it depends on discipline, whether prescribed by the Shari'ah or not, such as various kinds of ta'zir (discretionary punishment), they should carry it out. If it depends on appointing people to take charge of it, that is required. And similarly for whatever else the enjoining of good and forbidding of evil cannot be completed without. ﴿And to God belongs the outcome of affairs﴾; that is, all affairs return to God, and He has informed us that the good outcome belongs to the God-fearing. So whoever God empowers over His servants, of the kings, and who carries out God's command, will have the praiseworthy outcome and the rightly guided condition. But whoever rules over them by tyranny and establishes among them the desires of his own soul, even if he attains a temporary kingship, his outcome is not praiseworthy; his rule is ill-omened and his end is blameworthy.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 22, verses 42–46:

{42–44} Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "If these polytheists deny you, then you are not the first messenger to be denied, and they are not the first nation to deny its messenger. {Before them, the people of Noah, ʿAd, and Thamud denied, and the people of Abraham, and the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan (Midian)}, that is, the people of Shuʿayb. {And Moses was denied, so I gave respite to the disbelievers}, those who denied, and I did not hasten the punishment against them, but I granted them respite until they persisted in their transgression, wandering blindly, and kept increasing in their disbelief and evil. {Then I seized them}, with punishment, the seizing of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. {So how was My rejection}, that is, how was My denunciation of their disbelief and their denial? It was the most severe of punishments and the most dreadful of retributions. Some of them I drowned; some were seized by the Blast; some were destroyed by the barren wind; some had the earth swallow them up; and some had the punishment of the Day of the Canopy sent upon them. So let these deniers take warning from them, lest what befell them befall them, for they are no better than them, and no exemption has been written for them in the revealed Books of Allah. And how many punished and destroyed people like these there have been!

{45} For this reason He says: {How many a town}, that is, how many a town, {We destroyed}, with severe punishment and worldly humiliation, {while it was wrongdoing}, through its disbelief in Allah and its denial of His messengers. Our punishment of it was not an injustice on Our part. {So it lies fallen upon its roofs}, that is, their dwellings lie in ruins, their palaces and walls collapsed, fallen upon their roofs, becoming desolate after having been populated, and lonely after having been inhabited by their people. {And many a well abandoned, and a lofty palace}, that is, how many a well once crowded with people drawing water for themselves and their livestock has been left without its people, with neither arrivals nor departures! And how many a palace its people toiled to build, raise, fortify and adorn, yet when the command of Allah came, it availed them nothing, and it became empty of its inhabitants. They became a lesson for whoever takes heed and an example for whoever reflects and considers.

{46} For this reason Allah calls His servants to travel through the earth so that they may look and take heed. He says: {Have they not travelled through the earth}, with their bodies and their hearts, {so that they might have hearts with which to understand}, the signs of Allah, and reflect with them upon the places of His lessons, {or ears with which to hear}, the reports of the earlier nations and the accounts of the punished generations. Otherwise, mere sight of the eye, hearing of the ear, and travel of the body devoid of reflection and taking heed is neither beneficial nor a means to the desired goal. For this reason He says: {Indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded}, that is, this harmful blindness in religion is blindness of the heart to the truth, so that it does not perceive it, just as a blind person does not see visible things. As for blindness of the eye, its end is merely a worldly sustenance and benefit.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 58–59:

{58} This is a great glad tiding for those who emigrate in the way of Allah, leaving their homes, their homeland, their children and their wealth, seeking the countenance of Allah and supporting the religion of Allah. The reward of such a person has become binding upon Allah, whether he dies in his bed or is killed striving in the way of Allah. {Allah will surely provide for them a goodly provision}: in the barzakh (the intermediate state) and on the Day of Resurrection, by entry into the Garden, which combines comfort, fragrance, beauty, goodness, and delight of heart and body. So let no one imagine that if he leaves his homes and wealth he will become poor and in need, for his Provider is the best of providers. This has indeed come to pass as He foretold: the foremost emigrants left their homes, their children and their wealth in support of the religion of Allah, and they had not waited long before Allah opened the lands to them and empowered them over the people, and they gathered from their wealth, so that they became among the richest of people.

If he does so, there is no blame upon him, and he is not to be censured. But if he is transgressed against after this, then Allah will surely aid him, because he is wronged. It is not permissible that he be transgressed against on account of having taken his right. And since Allah aids the one who requites another for his wrongdoing when he is wronged afterward, then the one who originally did not punish anyone when he was wronged and aggressed against is even closer to being helped.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ That is: He pardons the sinners, so He does not hasten to punish them, and He forgives their sins, removing them and their effects from them. {67} God informs us that He has appointed for every community a way of worship (*mansak*), meaning a place and manner of worship, which may differ in some matters while all agree on justice and wisdom. So no law of any of the laws may be objected to, especially by the unlettered (*ummiyyun*), the people of polytheism and manifest ignorance. For this reason He says: ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾, meaning the deniers do not dispute with you and object to some of what you brought them with their corrupt intellects, such as their dispute over the lawfulness of carrion through their corrupt analogy. They say: "You eat what you kill, but you do not eat what God kills?!" And like their saying: ﴿Trade is only like usury﴾ [2:275], and similar objections whose particulars need not be answered. They deny the very principle of prophethood, and there is no argument or debate in them on their own. Rather, every situation has its own speech. So you are certain of your affair and sure of your religion, and this necessitates for you firmness and proceeding with what your Lord has commanded you. You are not upon a matter that is doubtful, nor a fabricated narrative, so that you would stand with people, their desires, and their opinions, and their objections would hold you back. For guidance is a description of everything the Messenger brought, and guidance is that by which guidance is attained in matters of foundations and branches, which are the matters whose goodness, justice, and wisdom are known through reason and the sound *fitrah* (innate human disposition). This is known through reflection upon the details of what is commanded and forbidden.

{68–69} For this reason God commanded him to turn away from their argument in this situation, saying: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: God knows best what you do﴾, meaning He knows your intentions and purposes, and will requite you for them on the Day of Resurrection, when God will judge between you ﴿concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾. Whoever conformed to the straight path is among the people of bliss, and whoever deviated from it is among the people of Hellfire.

Therefore He mentioned the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His Book, saying: ﴿Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth?﴾ Nothing is hidden from Him of it, whether apparent matters or hidden ones, the obscure and the evident, the earlier and the later. That all-encompassing knowledge of what is in the heaven and the earth has been recorded by God in a Book, namely the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*), when God created the pen (*al-qalam*). He said to it: "Write!" It said: "What shall I write?" He said: "Write what will happen until the Day of Resurrection." ﴿Indeed that is easy for God﴾, even if its comprehension is not encompassed by you; God finds it easy to encompass all things in knowledge and to record that in a Book that accords with reality.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 71–72:

{71} He, exalted is He, mentions the state of those who associate partners with Him and set others equal to Him, and that their state is the most wretched of states, and that they have no basis for what they do. They have no knowledge of it; rather, it is mere imitation (taqlid) that they received from their misguided forefathers. A person may have no knowledge of what he does, while in reality he has a proof for it that he does not know. Here He informs that Allah has not sent down in this any {sultan}, i.e., any proof that indicates it and makes it permissible; rather, He has sent down decisive evidences refuting its corruption and falsehood. Then He threatened the wrongdoers among them, the obstinate opponents of the truth, saying: {And for the wrongdoers there is no helper}: no one will help them against the punishment of Allah when it descends upon them and befalls them.

{72} Do these people, who have no knowledge of what they are upon, have any intention to follow the signs and the guidance when it comes to them, or are they content with the falsehood they are upon? He mentions this in His saying: {And when Our signs are recited to them}: which are the glorious signs of Allah that necessitate the clarification of truth from falsehood; they do not pay attention to them, nor do they raise their heads to them. Rather, {you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the denial}: of their hatred and aversion towards them. You see their faces frowning and their skins darkened. {They nearly assault those who recite Our signs to them}; i.e., they nearly inflict upon them killing and severe beating, out of the intensity of their hatred for them, and their hatred for the truth and their enmity towards it. This state of the disbelievers is evil, and its evil is an evil indeed. But there is something worse than it: the state to which they will return. Therefore He said: {Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination."} Its evil is long and broad, and its hardships and pains increase continually.

This is a parable that God struck to illustrate the ugliness of worshipping idols, to show the deficiency of the minds of those who worship them, and the weakness of all of them. He says:

﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it.﴾ This is an address to both believers and disbelievers. The believers increase in knowledge and insight, while upon the disbelievers the proof is established. ﴿A parable is presented, so listen to it﴾: that is, give it your ears, understand what it contains, and do not come to it with heedless hearts and turned-away ears; rather, give it your hearts and your ears. It is this:

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides God﴾ includes everything that is invoked besides God. ﴿Will never create a fly﴾: which is among the lowest and most despicable of creatures. So they do not have the power to create this weak creature, and what is above it is more so. ﴿Even if they gathered together for it﴾. Rather, even more than that: ﴿and if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from it﴾. This is the utmost of impotence. ﴿Weak is the seeker and the sought﴾: the seeker being the one worshipped besides God, and the sought being the fly. Each of them is weak, and weaker than both is the one who clings to this weak creature and places it in the station of the Lord of the worlds. This is how they have failed to measure God with His true measure, when they equated the poor, powerless one in every respect with the rich, powerful One in every respect. They equated one who owns for himself and for others neither benefit nor harm, neither death nor life nor resurrection, with the One who is the Benefiter, the Harmer, the Giver, the Withholder, the Owner of the dominion and the One who disposes of it in every kind of disposal.

﴿Indeed, God is Powerful, Mighty﴾: that is, of complete strength and complete might. From the completeness of His strength and might: the forelocks of all creation are in His hand, and no mover moves nor any still thing is still except by His will and wish. Whatever God wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. And from the completeness of His strength: He holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease. And from the completeness of His strength: He will raise all creation, first and last, with a single cry. And from the completeness of His strength: He destroyed the tyrants and the rebellious nations with a small thing, and a lash of His punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 75–76:

{75–76} When Allah (Exalted is He) had explained His perfection and the weakness of the idols, and that He alone is truly worthy of worship, He then explained the state of the messengers and how they are distinguished from the rest of creation by the virtues with which they were distinguished. He said: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾. That is, He selects and chooses messengers from among the angels, and messengers from among mankind, who are the purest of their kind, the most complete in the attributes of glory, and the most deserving of being chosen. The messengers are none other than the elite of creation in every respect. The One who chose and selected them is not ignorant of the realities of things, nor does He know some things and not others. Indeed, the One who chooses them is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, whose knowledge, hearing and sight encompass all things. Thus His choosing them is based on His knowledge that they are worthy of that, and that revelation is suitable for them, as He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾; that is, He sends the messengers to call people to Allah. Among them are those who respond, those who reject their call, those who act upon it, and those who shun it. This is the function of the messengers. As for the recompense for those deeds, their outcome is with Allah, and they will not lose from Him either bounty or justice.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 22, verses 77–78:

(77) Allah the Exalted commands His believing servants to pray, and He singles out bowing (rukū') and prostration (sujūd) from it, for their excellence, for their being pillars of the prayer, and because worship is the coolness of the eyes and the solace of the grieving heart. His lordship and His kindness toward the servants require that they devote their worship sincerely to Him, and He commands them to do good in general. Allah has linked success to these matters, saying: ﴿So that you may prosper﴾. That is: you will attain the desired goal and be saved from the feared harm. There is no path to success except sincerity in worshipping the Creator and striving to benefit His servants. Whoever is granted this success has been given the full cup of happiness, prosperity and triumph.

(78) ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾. Jihad (striving, exerting one's utmost effort) is the expenditure of one's full capacity to achieve the sought objective. Striving for Allah with the striving due to Him is the complete standing by the command of Allah and the calling of creation to His path by every means that leads to it: by sincere counsel, teaching, fighting, disciplining, admonishing, exhortation and other means. ﴿He has chosen you﴾. That is: He has chosen you, O assembly of Muslims, from among the people, chose the religion for you, was pleased with it for you, and chose for you the best of books and the best of messengers. So respond to this great favor by standing firmly in striving for Him with the striving due to Him.

Since His saying ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾ might lead someone to think that this is a case of imposing what cannot be borne or what is hardship, He guarded against this by saying: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾. That is: no difficulty or hardship. Rather, He made it easy to the utmost degree and facilitated it with the utmost facility. First, He commanded and obligated only what is easy for souls, which does not weigh them down or overburden them. Then, if some causes requiring relief arise, He lightens what He commanded, either by dropping it entirely or by dropping part of it.

From this verse a legal principle is derived: "hardship brings about facilitation" and "necessities permit what is forbidden." Much of the subsidiary rulings enter under this, as is well known in the books of jurisprudence.

﴿The religion of your father Abraham﴾. That is: this religion mentioned and these commands described are the religion of your father Abraham, upon which he remained. So hold fast to it and keep to it. ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾. That is: you are mentioned and famous in the earlier books. ﴿And in this﴾, that is, in this Book and this law, this name has been yours since old times and recently. ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ concerning your deeds, good and bad. ﴿And that you may be witnesses over the people﴾, by virtue of your being the best nation brought forth for mankind, a justly balanced, excellent, moderate nation. You bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed to their peoples, and you bear witness against the nations that their messengers conveyed to them, according to what Allah has told you in His Book.

﴿So establish the prayer﴾ with its pillars, conditions, limits and all its requirements. ﴿And give zakat﴾ (obligatory almsgiving) to its rightful recipients, in thankfulness to Allah for what He has bestowed upon you. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾. That is: take refuge in Him and rely upon Him in this, and do not rely upon your own strength and power. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, who manages your affairs, directs you with His excellent management, and disposes you according to His best decree. ﴿How excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper﴾. That is: an excellent Protector for whoever takes Him as protector so that he attains his goal, and an excellent Helper for whoever seeks His help so that He repels harm from him.

The commentary on Surah al-Hajj is complete. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
